title: SAT Equivalent Expressions: Factoring, Exponents, and the Plug-In Check
description:
"Which expression is equivalent?" questions come from a short list of algebra tools, and the wrong answers come from a short list of mistakes. This lesson covers both, then works through 7 SAT-style practice questions that get harder as they go.

You'll learn:
• Distributing (especially a negative) and combining like terms
• Factoring: greatest common factor, difference of squares, trinomials, and grouping
• Exponent rules, including negative and fractional exponents and radicals
• Adding and simplifying rational expressions
• Matching coefficients to find a missing constant
• The plug-in check and the Desmos check for any equivalence question
• The 4 traps behind most wrong answers

All questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (Advanced Math, skill: Equivalent expressions).
